# Temple Scroll Column 30 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 30 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**30:1** You shall make an outer court. On the south side, the outer court shall extend one thousand six hundred cubits from corner to corner.

**30:2** From the southeastern corner going westward along the south side to the southwestern corner.

**30:3** You shall make three gates on the south side, equally spaced from one another and from the corners.

**30:4** The gates shall be forty-two cubits wide and twenty-eight cubits high to the lintel.

**30:5** Each gate shall have a porch, forty-two cubits wide and twenty-eight cubits deep, with towers upon the gates.

**30:6** On the east side, the outer court shall extend one thousand six hundred cubits from corner to corner.

**30:7** From the southeastern corner going northward along the east side to the northeastern corner.

**30:8** You shall make three gates on the east side, equally spaced from one another and from the corners.

**30:9** The gates shall have the same dimensions: forty-two cubits wide and twenty-eight cubits high.

**30:10** Each gate shall have a porch of the same dimensions, with towers upon them.

**30:11** On the north side, the outer court shall extend one thousand six hundred cubits, from the northeastern corner going westward to the northwestern corner.

**30:12** You shall make three gates on the north side, equally spaced from one another and from the corners, with the same dimensions.

**30:13** On the west side, the outer court shall extend one thousand six hundred cubits, from the northwestern corner going southward to the southwestern corner.

**30:14** You shall make three gates on the west side, equally spaced from one another and from the corners, with the same dimensions.

**30:15** The total perimeter of the outer court shall be six thousand four hundred cubits, a square from corner to corner.

**30:16** The wall of the outer court shall be seven cubits thick and forty-nine cubits high, built upon foundations of hewn stone sunk three cubits into the ground.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus translation of Column 30. "Porch" maintained over LOGOS's "portico" and PNEUMA's "entrance hall" per project convention. "Towers" preferred over PNEUMA's "watchtowers" — the Hebrew does not specify a surveillance function. The outer court's extraordinary scale (1,600 cubits per side, approximately 730 meters) confirms the Temple Scroll's idealized, eschatological character. Twelve gates (three per side) correspond to the twelve tribes.*
